name: RISD Museum
unique: A design school museum with a 12th century French chapel, a Mesopotamian lion, Gorham silver and a room of student work, all in a block of College Hill.
buzz: The decorative arts and the costume galleries are quietly excellent; the museum is free on Sundays and students use it as a study hall.

name: Benefit Street Mile of History
unique: A mile of original colonial and federal houses on College Hill, with the First Baptist Church in America at one end and a burial ground where Roger Williams is remembered.
buzz: The street itself is free and the best architecture walk in the state; the Athenaeum and the John Brown House are the paid stops.

name: The Breakers
customer: House tour people, architecture fans, families
unique: The Vanderbilt summer cottage of 70 rooms, with a great hall of Caen limestone, a dining room that took a year to carve and a cliff walk terrace over the Atlantic.
buzz: The audio tour is better than the guided one for the details; buy the multi house ticket if you are doing two or three.

name: Ocean Drive
unique: Ten miles of coastal road past Gilded Age cottages, rocky coves, Brenton Point and the entrance to the Cliff Walk, with the ocean on one side and stone walls on the other.
buzz: Drive it at sunset and stop at Brenton Point; cyclists do the loop in summer and the road is narrow in places.

name: Watch Hill Carousel
unique: A flying horse carousel built in 1879 hanging from chains rather than mounted on a frame, still turning beside a Rhode Island beach.
buzz: Collectors say it is one of the oldest in the country; the ride is two dollars and the beach and lighthouse are a short walk.

name: Misquamicut State Beach
unique: A wide barrier beach with real surf, a boardwalk of food stands and the Atlantic on one side and a salt pond on the other.
buzz: It is the busiest beach in the state and the surf is the draw; arrive before nine or park in the private lots across the road.

name: Blithewold Mansion
unique: A 45 room summer mansion on Narragansett Bay with a 10 acre arboretum, a giant sequoia and a bamboo grove, all on a lawn that runs to the water.
buzz: Gardeners come for the rare trees and the spring bulb show; the house tour is short and the grounds are the reason to stay.

name: Herreshoff Marine Museum
customer: Sailors, boat builders, America's Cup fans
unique: The boatyard where Captain Nat Herreshoff built six America's Cup defenders, with a model room, the catamarans of 1988 and a working waterfront.
buzz: Sailing people treat it as a shrine and non sailors are converted by the model room; the restored boats are in the water in summer.

name: Bristol Fourth of July Parade
unique: The oldest continuous Fourth of July celebration in the country, a morning parade down Hope Street past colonial houses with the nation's oldest flag still flying.
buzz: Locals claim their spot the night before; parking is impossible and the walk from the edge of town is part of the ritual.

name: Goddard Memorial State Park
unique: Nearly 500 acres on Greenwich Bay with a beach, a bridle path, a picnic grove and one of the few public polo fields in New England.
buzz: The beach is calm and shallow and the park is quiet on weekdays; the polo matches in summer are free to watch.

name: Nathanael Greene Homestead
customer: Rev war people, history families, locals
unique: The Georgian house Washington's most trusted general built and left to go to war, with period rooms and a forge site on the grounds.
buzz: The volunteers know Greene's campaigns in detail; it is small and only open seasonally, so call before driving.

name: Conimicut Point Park
unique: A sandbar point at the mouth of the Providence River with a view of the Conimicut lighthouse and the bay traffic, a favorite for sitting in the car at dusk.
buzz: Locals come for the sunset and the fishing; the tide comes in fast across the point and there is no lifeguard.

name: Church Street Marketplace
unique: Four blocks of brick street closed to cars, with a farmers market, buskers, a used bookstore and the lake at the bottom of the hill.
buzz: The summer festival and the winter lights are the two seasons; locals walk it fast and visitors should take the side streets to the lake.

name: Burlington Bike Path
unique: A paved eight mile path along Lake Champlain with beaches, a skate park, a fishing pier and a view of the Adirondacks across the water.
buzz: The north beach and the causeway are the stops; the path is flat and the lake is swimmable in July and August.

name: Vermont State House
customer: Statehouse collectors, school groups, history people
unique: A granite capitol with a gold leaf dome and a cedar statue of Ceres on top, in a town of 8,000 that is the smallest state capital in the country.
buzz: Tours are free and the Representatives Hall is the room to see; the farmers market on the lawn in summer is the local ritual.

name: Cabot Creamery
unique: A farmer owned dairy cooperative with a visitor center over the cheese plant, a tasting counter and the world's best selling cheddar made a few feet away.
buzz: The tasting is generous and the tour is short; the shop sells a 10 year cheddar you cannot get at home.

name: Mount Philo
unique: The first state park in Vermont, a 968 foot peak with a road and a trail to a summit view of Lake Champlain and the Adirondacks.
buzz: The hike is 45 minutes and the view is the best effort to reward ratio in the state; the road is narrow and the lot fills on fall weekends.

name: Rokeby Museum
customer: History people, students, abolition history fans
unique: A Quaker farm that was a stop on the Underground Railroad, with four generations of family letters, a stone barn and a trail through the fields.
buzz: The letters are the exhibit and the guides read them aloud; it is small and the story is specific and local.

name: Bennington Battle Monument
customer: History people, families, state monument collectors
unique: A 306 foot stone obelisk, the tallest structure in Vermont, with an elevator to an observation deck over three states and the site of the 1777 battle.
buzz: The elevator is a surprise in a 19th century monument; the view from the top and the museum at the base are both quick.

name: Hildene
unique: Robert Todd Lincoln's 24 room Georgian mansion with the original 1908 Aeolian organ, formal gardens and a working goat dairy on 400 acres.
buzz: The organ plays on a schedule and the goat dairy is the family draw; the view of the Taconic and Green mountains is the postcard.

name: Hogback Mountain
unique: A roadside pull off at 2,400 feet on Route 9 with a long view into the Green Mountains and a trail along the ridge.
buzz: The first week of October is the reason to come; the pull off is small and the trail is a gentle walk along the top.

name: Marlboro Music Festival
customer: Chamber music people, students, summer visitors
unique: A summer chamber music school where established players and young musicians rehearse together in a barn and perform programs they chose the week before.
buzz: Audiences say the rehearsals are as good as the concerts and some are open; tickets are cheap for the quality and the barn is unheated.

name: Killington
unique: The biggest vertical drop in the east and the longest season, with 155 trails across six peaks and a gondola that runs in summer for leaf peepers.
buzz: Skiers argue about the crowds but agree on the terrain; midweek in March is the locals' window and the access road is a long drive from anywhere.

name: Vermont Marble Museum
unique: A museum in a working marble company town, with the world's largest marble exhibit, a quarry overlook and the tomb of a company president cut into a block of stone.
buzz: The carving demos and the quarry view are the highlights; the town itself is built of marble and the museum is a labor of local pride.

name: Trapp Family Lodge
customer: Sound of Music fans, cross country skiers, families
unique: The Austrian lodge the von Trapp family built after fleeing Europe, with a meadow, a beer hall, cross country ski trails and a weekly history talk by a family member.
buzz: The story is the draw and the trails are excellent; the visit is free if you are eating or skiing and the family talks book out.

name: Smugglers' Notch
unique: A family ski mountain in a notch where boulders pinch the road and the trails run through birch and hemlock, with a summer water park and zip line.
buzz: Parents like the ski school and the slope side lodging; the notch road is closed in winter and the drive around is long.

name: Snow Farm Vineyard
unique: A vineyard on a Lake Champlain island with a tasting room in a barn and free summer concerts on the lawn overlooking the water and the Adirondacks.
buzz: The Thursday concerts are the local summer tradition; the wine is cold climate and the view beats it.

name: Lake Champlain Islands Bike Loop
unique: A flat loop across the islands of Lake Champlain on quiet roads, with orchards, a ferry crossing and water on both sides most of the way.
buzz: The islands are flat and the traffic is light; the apple orchards in September and the ferry back to New York are the local route.

name: Great Vermont Corn Maze
unique: A 24 acre corn maze cut with a different design each year, plus a smaller maze for children and a cow train, on a working Vermont farm.
buzz: Adults get lost for two hours and children do the small maze; wear closed shoes and go early, the field is hot in September.

name: Silvio O. Conte National Wildlife Refuge
unique: The Nulhegan Basin division, 26,000 acres of boreal forest and bog in the Northeast Kingdom where moose, black bear and spruce grouse live and the Connecticut River begins.
buzz: Birders come for spruce grouse and gray jay; the driving loop is gravel and the trails are flat and buggy in June.
